Title: Comments on: AI-Reddit study leader gets warning as ethics committee moves to ‘stricter review process’
Comments on: AI-Reddit study leader gets warning as ethics committee moves to ‘stricter review process’  https://retractionwatch.com/2025/04/29/ethics-committee-ai-llm-reddit-changemyview-university-zurich/ Tracking retractions as a window into the scientific process Sun, 05 Apr 2026 02:54:40 +0000  hourly   1  https://wordpress.org/? v=6.9.4   By: ruth  https://retractionwatch.com/2025/04/29/ethics-committee-ai-llm-reddit-changemyview-university-zurich/#comment-2378366 Sun, 05 Apr 2026 02:54:40 +0000 https://retractionwatch.com/? p=131750#comment-2378366 In reply to Liz. which law should make the opinion of the ethics committe of a university binding? ]]>    By: DS  https://retractionwatch.com/2025/04/29/ethics-committee-ai-llm-reddit-changemyview-university-zurich/#comment-2343599 Tue, 29 Jul 2025 23:04:58 +0000 https://retractionwatch.com/? p=131750#comment-2343599 In reply to Liz. Sounds like the ethics committee is trying to absolve themselves of any responsibility. ]]>    By: DS  https://retractionwatch.com/2025/04/29/ethics-committee-ai-llm-reddit-changemyview-university-zurich/#comment-2343598 Tue, 29 Jul 2025 23:03:40 +0000 https://retractionwatch.com/? p=131750#comment-2343598 The PI was formally warned – but who is it??? ]]>    By: Liz  https://retractionwatch.com/2025/04/29/ethics-committee-ai-llm-reddit-changemyview-university-zurich/#comment-2334669 Sat, 03 May 2025 13:31:46 +0000 https://retractionwatch.com/? p=131750#comment-2334669 I would like to hear the opinion of U Zurich and the Swiss government on the following statement from the U spox:. “Recommendations from the ethics committees are not legally binding, Ziegler said. “The researchers themselves are responsible for carrying out the project and publishing the results.”. Ethics committees and IRBs review proposed research with humans and make determinations, i.e. decline to approve, approve or approve with conditions/required revisions. These bodies are not advisory where law requires ethical approval, and researchers have an obligation to obtain it. Protocol changes post-approval also require review & approval. Either the protocol was approved, revised or otherwise, or it wasn’t. From the post above it’s unclear if the ethics committee approved the research. If ethics committees are merely advisory bodies, this is an absolute bar to cooperative research with Swiss institutions. I hope there’s some miscommunication because it would be very troubling if researchers could do whatever they wished by simply declining “advice.”.
